text:
maya: hey, spotting a weird tail-latency spike on AMD nodes after last night's runtime rollout. seq_len=8 p50 ok, p99 up ~3-4x. Seen on two different customers. :thinking:

maya: quick grep of logs shows repeated fallbacks to cpu_matmul for a subset of requests, even though nodes have rocm kernels installed.

maya: snippet from the runtime log: 
```
2026-05-02T03:12:44Z INFO route_decision: preferred_kernel=fused_attn_rocm_v2 available=false -> fallback=cpu_matmul
2026-05-02T03:12:44Z WARN kv_cache: cache_miss_on_route_handoff request_id=...
```

david: ugh. looks like the kernel registry didn't advertise the new fused_attn_rocm_v2 artifact to some shards during the canary.

david: can you paste full node tags where you saw it? gpu.arch and driver versions please.

maya: two nodes: amd-gpu-p4x-03 (gfx90a rocm5.5), amd-gpu-p4x-07 (gfx90a rocm5.5). both report kernel list missing fused_attn_rocm_v2 but have attn_rocm_v1 and scalar_fallback.

cheng: hmm this smells like a packaging name mismatch during the build -> registry publish step. packaging produced fused_attn_rocm_v2-optimized but registry key was fused_attn_rocm_v2. our conditional routing does strict name matching today.

alex: consequence is worse because we do a runtime handoff: if preferred kernel missing we reroute to a compatible-but-slower path. that path doesn't support kv-cache hotload so KV pages are re-materialized per-step causing extra mem copies. hence p99 shot up.

maya: profiler snapshot attached (paste):
```
flamegraph:
 - step 0..4: rocm_dispatch (20%)
 - step 5..10: cpu_matmul (60%)
 - step 11..20: kv_cache_rebuild (15%)
```

maya: note kv_cache_rebuild is the expensive one for short sequences. tiny overhead per-token but aggregated at tail.

david: for context, our routing code picks kernel by (model_variant, seq_len_bucket, device_features). if kernel not found we call find_compatible() which currently prefers same-arch kernels, else falls back to cpu. the compatible set didn't include alternate rocm name forms.

tanya: short-term mitigation ideas: 1) lax name matching (strip suffixes), 2) prefer any rocm kernel for seq_len<=32, 3) preserve kv-cache compatibility by honoring cache layout transformation when handoff happens.

cheng: option 1 is low risk: add normalization mapping at registry lookup: canonicalize names, also keep alias table. this fixes cases where build suffixes differ.

alex: option 2 also easy but might route to a slower rocm variant for large seqs; need seq_len-aware policy. maybe: if seq_len<=32 allow any rocm kernel, else require exact match.

maya: can we detect kv-cache incompatibility during handoff? e.g., when route changes, validate kv_layout version; if mismatch, prefer other kernels or trigger fast-transform instead of full rebuild.

david: yes the route decision could return a handoff_hint object that includes kv_compat boolean. if false, runtime can either skip handoff or run a lightweight transform (we have a thin path in transform-service).

tanya: telemetry gap: we don't have metric for "kernel_alias_mismatch" or "kv_rebuild_after_handoff". we need those to quantify impact and alert.

alex: I'll add two metrics: runtime.kernel_lookup.alias_fallback and runtime.kv.handoff_rebuild_count with tags {node, model_variant, seq_len_bucket}.

maya: testing: I reproduced locally by renaming a kernel in /opt/rocm/kernels and forcing registry to not match. confirm behavior.

cheng: potential long-term: autotuner should include an alias table derived from build metadata, and the compilation pipeline should publish both canonical and short names. also add a registry healthcheck that compares published kernels vs installed artifacts across shards.

david: for immediate patch: I'll submit a tiny runtime PR to normalize kernel names and add alias_fallback metric. also gating: if alias_fallback && kv_incompatible -> do not fallback to cpu; instead try other rocm variants or fail fast for caller to retry.

maya: please include a canary rule in the PR so we don't regress new nodes. we want to roll to non-prod first.

infra-bot: deploy: started canary deployment of runtime@edge-fix-aliases to env=staging at 2026-05-02T04:10Z :rocket:

alex: thx infra-bot. tanya/cheng, can you add a quick e2e that simulates missing kernel name and checks kv_cache consistency after handoff? 10-15 min test.

tanya: on it. I'll also add a perf test for seq_len buckets [8,16,64] to capture regressions.

cheng: FYI I dug into build logs: the build script started appending -optimized on May 1st for rocm kernels only. that's why aliasing broke. patching build pipeline to include alias symlink.

maya: ok roadmap: (1) runtime alias normalization PR (david) (2) metrics + canary (alex) (3) build pipeline alias fix (cheng) (4) e2e/perf tests (tanya). owners assigned.

david: I'll open the PR and link it here in 15m.

maya: thanks, appreciate the quick triage. let's monitor p99 after canary. :thumbsup:
